name: Eilean Siar (Na h-Eileanan Siar)
title: The Outer Hebrides —
tagline: Callanish, Harris Tweed and the Gaelic heartland of Scotland.
summary: Na h-Eileanan Siar, the Western Isles or Outer Hebrides, stretches 130 miles from the Butt of Lewis to Barra Head. It is the strongest remaining area of Scottish Gaelic, with over half the population speaking it.
The islands have white sandy beaches, the Callanish Standing Stones, and the weaving of Harris Tweed.

famous_for.title: Harris Tweed
famous_for.text: A handwoven cloth protected by an Act of Parliament.

famous_for.title: Gaelic
famous_for.text: The language is heard daily in shops, schools and churches.

places.name: Callanish Standing Stones
places.text: A cross-shaped stone setting older than Stonehenge.

places.name: Luskentyre Beach
places.text: A huge white beach with turquoise water.

places.name: Barra Airport
places.text: The only airport with a beach runway used for scheduled flights.

festivals.name: Hebridean Celtic Festival
festivals.text: A music festival in the grounds of Lews Castle.

festivals.name: Royal National Mòd
festivals.text: The Gaelic festival, held in different places each year.

sport.intro: Football, shinty and sailing are popular in the islands.

community.intro: Gaelic-speaking families from the Western Isles settled in Nova Scotia, Cape Breton and Australia, and Gaelic still survives in parts of Canada.

ancestry: Searching for your family's roots? ScotlandsPeople, the Scottish Government's genealogy service, holds statutory registers of births, marriages and deaths, census returns and Old Parish Registers.
